videos.title: Yellowstone's Wolf Planners Expected a Third of Wolves to Add Nothing
videos.description:
In 1994, U.S. officials approved returning gray wolves to Yellowstone after a formal environmental impact statement. The planners expected about a third of released wolves to add nothing to population growth, but the 1995 founders reproduced more, died less, and roamed less than assumed, so planned Canadian transplants were judged unnecessary by 1997. #YellowstoneWolves #WildlifeHistory #EnvironmentalHistory

videos.title: Railroad Clocks Ran on Standard Time 35 Years Before U.S. Law Did
videos.description:
Before standard time, American cities set their clocks by the sun. At noon on November 18, 1883, railroad clocks across the United States were reset to a new standard time, and several cities heard noon strike twice. Congress did not pass its Standard Time Act until 1918.
#history #timezones #railroads

videos.title: The Smithsonian Began as a Backup Plan in One Man's Will
videos.description:
James Smithson's will left most of his estate to his nephew, with a backup clause in case the nephew died without heirs. When that happened in 1835, the money went to the United States to found the Smithsonian Institution, after Congress decided whether to accept it. Smithson's reason for choosing the United States remains unknown.
#history #smithsonian #didyouknow

videos.title: Sichuan's Ancient Water Scheme Manages a River Without Blocking It
videos.description:
Dujiangyan, in Sichuan Province, China, is an ancient irrigation system that controls the Minjiang River without a dam across it. Engineers used dikes, a floodgate and a diversion passage to split the flow and keep water reaching the Chengdu Plain's farmland. UNESCO documents the system, which still supplies farms today. #ChinaHistory #IrrigationHistory #IngeniousSolutions

videos.description:

videos.title: Apollo 13's Square Air Canisters Did Not Fit the Round Openings
videos.description:
On Apollo 13 in 1970, spare square carbon dioxide canisters from the command module could not connect to the lunar module's round scrubber ports. Houston teams tested a workaround in an altitude chamber, and the crew built it from a suit hose, plastic bags, a cue card and duct tape. NASA's technical brief records that carbon dioxide then fell to 1 mmHg.
#Apollo13 #SpaceHistory #NASAHistory

videos.description:

Some framed prints there had been bubble-wrapped for shipping, and the wrap helped keep them from sinking, though water still damaged the edges. This is one documented studio case, not proof of how bubble wrap performs in floods generally.

videos.title: The Panama Canal Builders Bought Wire Screens Against Mosquitoes
videos.description:
In the early 1900s, the US canal project in Panama faced yellow fever and malaria among its workers. Investigators had linked the fever to mosquitoes breeding in standing water, and the Isthmian Canal Commission chose to pay for wire screens rather than save the money. Sources credit the sanitation program led by William Gorgas as a major factor in completing the canal, though not its only cause. #PanamaCanal #WorldHistory #Sanitation

videos.title: Before Nigeria's Presidency, What Was Nnamdi Azikiwe Really Doing?
videos.description:
Nigeria's first president is often remembered for politics, but his early public career was built on newspapers. This short Behind the Legend story looks at how printing shaped his path to leadership. #NigerianHistory #WestAfricanHistory #BehindTheLegend

videos.title: Why Did India's Freedom Walk Start With Salt?
videos.description:
In British-ruled India, the Salt Act made making your own salt illegal, touching every household. In 1930, Mohandas Gandhi walked to the sea to defy that rule and turned a kitchen staple into a symbol of self-rule. #IndianHistory #WorldHistory #Salt

videos.title: Why Can't Scholars Read a Script From Four Thousand Years Ago?
videos.description: The Indus civilisation left hundreds of short inscriptions on small carved seals, but no one has yet matched its signs to a known language. This Unsolved episode covers the evidence, the main explanations, and why the open question still matters. #IndusValley #AncientWriting #UnsolvedHistory
